identity.title: Photoperiodic responses persist in DH-like neuropeptide gene mutants of the band-legged ground cricket, Dianemobius nigrofasciatus.

content.abstract: Seasonal adaptation is essential for the survival and reproduction of organisms inhabiting environments with predictable annual fluctuations. Photoperiodism is a key adaptive mechanism that enables most multivoltine insects to synchronize physiological and developmental processes with seasonal environmental changes, yet its underlying endocrine mechanisms remain poorly understood. Diapause hormone (DH) and DH-like neuropeptides, which belong to the tryptopyrokinin (TPK) family and are characterized by a conserved C-terminal WFGPRXa motif, play a pivotal role in photoperiodically regulated maternal embryonic diapause induction in several insect species. In some lepidopteran insects, DH has also been implicated in the regulation of photoperiodic responses beyond diapause induction, raising the possibility that DH/DH-like neuropeptides function as a common regulator of multiple photoperiodic responses across insects. However, whether this mechanism is conserved across insect taxa remains unclear. The band-legged ground cricket Dianemobius nigrofasciatus exhibits multiple photoperiodic responses, including maternal embryonic diapause induction, wing morph and rate of nymphal development. Here, we investigated the involvement of DH-like neuropeptides in photoperiodic responses in D. nigrofasciatus. Two genes encoding TPKs were identified from the genome sequence of D. nigrofasciatus. One corresponded to capa, whereas the other was designated Din-dh because it encoded seven TPKs (i.e., DH-like neuropeptides). We established three mutant lines carrying distinct Din-dh alleles derived from two G(0) founders and investigated whether Din-dh is involved in photoperiodic responses. All mutant lines retained detectable photoperiodic responses. These results indicate that disruption of Din-dh does not abolish photoperiodic responses examined in D. nigrofasciatus.
